source.title: Infant language development is related to the acquisition of walking.

confidence_rationale: Walking onset was associated with a jump in receptive and productive vocabulary independent of age (longitudinal n=44, replicated age-held-constant n=75). This bears on A1's specificity clause: a motor milestone also tracks language, so play milestones would have to beat motor ones, not just correlate. Weight is limited because walking may act through social opportunities (the authors found social predictors of language only in walkers), which is partly compatible with MECH-308.
failure_signatures: Walking may change language via richer social and play interaction, making it a mediator for, not a competitor to, the play hypothesis.
Short age window (10-13.5 months) and parent-report vocabulary measures.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The acquisition of walking is associated with a significant increase in receptive and productive language independent of age, and in walking infants language is predicted by social-environment factors.
mapping.ree_translation: Challenges MECH-308 acceptance criterion A1, which requires language milestones to correlate more strongly with play milestones than with motor milestones at matched ages. A motor milestone showing an age-independent language link raises the bar for A1.
mapping.mapping_caveat: No direct head-to-head comparison of play vs motor milestones. Walle and Campos's own interpretation includes social mediation, which MECH-308 could absorb (locomotion opens play/joint-frame opportunities). PubMed lists the issue as 2014 volume 50 with 2013 e-publication; year recorded as 2014 print.
mapping.source_context: Two studies of typically developing infants 10-13.5 months; longitudinal biweekly and cross-sectional crawler vs walker comparison.

confidence_components.notes: Bears on the A1 specificity clause rather than the core mechanism.
